article.intro: In the Warriors books every Clan cat has a two-part name: a prefix that stays for life and a suffix that changes as the cat grows up. A kit called Yewkit becomes the apprentice Yewpaw, earns a warrior name like Yewsong and, if they lead their Clan, becomes Yewstar. This **warrior cat name generator** makes original names in that style for every rank, from a fur colour if you like, and can show a whole life from kit to warrior. It's a fan-made, unofficial tool inspired by Erin Hunter's Warriors books, and it never gives you the name of a cat from the books.

sections.heading: Eight good warrior cat names
sections.content:
All eight came from the generator, across ranks and fur colours:

  • Sootsong: a black warrior's name. The prefix describes the coat and the suffix the cat's voice.
  • Ravenlight: another black cat, with a bright suffix to balance the dark prefix.
  • Rustnose: a ginger warrior named for one feature, the way many book cats are.
  • Patchheart: a tortie or calico, named for a patched coat and a kind nature.
  • Whitedash: a white cat that moves fast.
  • Comfreydew: a medicine cat, named after a healing herb.
  • Ospreystar: a leader, with the -star every Clan leader takes.
  • Stillkit → Stillpaw → Stillfern → Stillstar: one cat's whole life, from kit to leader.

sections.heading: How warrior cat names are built
sections.content:
The Warriors series, first published in 2003 under the pen name Erin Hunter (several authors share it), gives every Clan cat a name in two halves:

  • The prefix is given at birth and kept for life. It usually comes from nature or from how the kit looks: a plant, a bird, a stone, a colour.
  • The suffix marks the cat's place in the Clan. Kits end in -kit and apprentices in -paw. A warrior's suffix is chosen at their naming ceremony, often for something about them: -song, -pelt, -fang.
  • Leaders replace their suffix with -star.

Choose a rank for the stage you need, or Whole life to see one cat grow up. Choose a fur colour for prefixes that suit the coat: soot, crow and raven for black cats, rust and fox for ginger ones, dapple and patch for torties. Choose With a Clan to add an original Clan name, like Maplelight of WolfClan.

sections.heading: Making your own Clan cat
sections.content:
• Look at the cat first. A prefix that describes the coat or the eyes makes the name feel earned.
  • Pick a suffix with a story. A warrior called -fang fights; one called -song is gentle. In the books the leader chooses it at the naming ceremony, so think about what they'd have seen.
  • Keep the Clan consistent. A Clan in pine woods might favour pine, needle and owl names.
  • Use it for your own cat too. The colour option makes it easy to find a name for a real black or ginger cat.

For more names for real cats, try the Black Cat Name Generator. For other animals, see all the animal name generators.

This is a fan-made generator, not connected to the Warriors books or their publishers. Every name here is original rather than taken from the books.

faqs.question: What are good warrior cat names?
faqs.answer: Two-part names from nature, like Sootsong, Ravenlight, Patchheart or Rustnose: a prefix for the cat's look and a suffix for its character. Choose a rank and a fur colour to get names like these.

faqs.question: How do warrior cat names work?
faqs.answer: A warrior name is a prefix plus a suffix, like Fern and song. Kits end in -kit, apprentices in -paw, and leaders swap their suffix for -star. The prefix never changes.

faqs.question: Can I use these names in my fan fiction?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every name here is original and checked against the cats in the books, so use them for your own Clan, story, roleplay or drawings.

faqs.question: What are good warrior cat names for a black cat?
faqs.answer: Names with a dark prefix, like Sootsong, Ravenlight, Crowspeck or Blackdawn. Choose Black under fur colour.
